title: Landing: fast-forward fails after main moves during the landing
lead: *Proposed.* A landing whose base moved after the merge-in merges it in again and retries the fast-forward once, instead of pausing; and the conflict-retry path takes the same steps as a first landing, so ork's own tracking commit is always followed by a merge-in.
findings_note: 2026-11-16, two landings paused on "git merge --ff-only B: ... Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded": S373 (run ork-20261116-155524-4cf4), after the orchestrator committed to main during the landing; S206 (run ork-20261116-172629-3a8b), after a merge conflict was resolved by hand and the run retried: ork's own commit d6b72802 "Tracking edits on main before landing S206" (`.slicer/log.jsonl`, one line) moved main, and the fast-forward then failed. A plain `ork retry` landed both.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: *Proposed.* `land` (`internal/engine/land.go:62-87`) commits tracking edits in `checkMain` and loops back to `mergeBaseIn`, but in the S206 case the fast-forward still ran against a base that had moved. Each such pause needs the owner or orchestrator to run `ork retry`, though nothing needs deciding.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestLandRemergesWhenBaseMovesBeforeFastForward`: a fake git where main gets one new commit after the merge-in lands the slice with a second merge-in and no pause.
- `TestLandAfterConflictRetryCommitsTrackingThenMerges`: a landing resumed after a resolved merge conflict, with a dirty `.slicer/log.jsonl` on main, commits it, merges main in again and fast-forwards.
- `TestLandPausesWhenBaseKeepsMoving`: a base that moves after every merge-in pauses after the second try with today's message.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Reproduce the S206 order in a test first; find why the merge-in did not follow the tracking commit.
2. Red tests above, then the fix.
3. Docs: `docs/design.md`. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.
